text.arabic_uthmani: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ۚ وَمَن يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ ۚ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًۭا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: direct vocative particle opening the command frame
words.prose: {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) begins by summoning the audience into direct command discourse. The three-layer believer-vocative formula gives the coming prohibition formal urgency and makes it a responsibility of the named faith-community, while the boundary from prior mercy into present agency prepares the ayah's later reminder that agency still depends on divine favor.

topics.headline: direct address before command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah begin as a summoned address, so the prohibition arrives as direct command discourse rather than detached description.
topics.reason: The particle opens the ayah and the following prohibition confirms the vocative command frame.

topics.headline: believer-vocative formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the three-layer believer-address formula as a recurring eligibility frame for the warning.
topics.reason: The row family ties the opening call to the known believer-vocative command formula.

topics.headline: shift from theology to agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a boundary move from prior divine mercy into a fresh demand on human agency that will be humbled later in the ayah.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect the opening summons to the discourse shift from declaration into command and dependence.

words.gloss_range: vocative intermediary with alerting force before the addressee is specified
words.prose: {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ayyuhā}}) works as the formal hinge of the address: the call has begun, but the exact addressee waits for the following believer qualifier. Its alerting force heightens attention before the prohibition arrives.

topics.headline: address delayed then specified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the address hold open for a moment before the believer qualifier resolves who is being called.
topics.reason: The intermediary form stands between the call particle and the relative qualifier.

topics.headline: alerting force in the address hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the call heightened by an alerting hinge before the prohibition appears.
topics.reason: The rows identify the final element as an attention-raising feature within the vocative formula.

words.gloss_range: definite plural relative pronoun filtering the summoned audience
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) filters the summoned audience through a definite plural relative clause. The command is not aimed at an isolated person or an undefined crowd; it addresses the known community constituted by belief.

topics.headline: definite relative filters the audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief is not background color; it is the identity condition for receiving the command.
topics.reason: The definite plural relative clause restricts the summoned audience before the prohibition.

topics.headline: plural communal addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command address a known community rather than an isolated individual.
topics.reason: The masculine plural relative form and definiteness support a known collective addressee.

words.gloss_range: completed Form IV believer-qualification before the prohibition
words.root_gloss_range: safety, trust, security, and belief field; local form names the already believing audience
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) completes the addressee identity as a prior, completed commitment, without adding a new object of belief inside this clause. The root's trust and security pressure makes the warning protective of an existing entrusted identity, and the formula joins wider believer-command usage (2:104; 5:1; 8:20).

topics.headline: completed belief as qualifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prohibition addressed to people already qualified by belief, with no new object of belief supplied in this clause.
topics.reason: The perfect plural verb completes the relative qualifier and omits an explicit complement.

topics.headline: trust and security pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses belief carrying trust and security pressure, while the local function remains the believer-label in the address.
topics.reason: The root family supports safety and trust pressure, but local grammar selects the completed believer qualifier.

topics.headline: believer formula and surah thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the address as part of a recurring command formula, with comparable uses at (2:104), (5:1), and (8:20).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete formula parallels and same-surah recurrence.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing the following jussive verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive here because it governs the following jussive verb. The ayah first issues binding authority and only then gives the conditional rationale, so explanation serves the command rather than replacing it.

topics.headline: prohibitive particle governs jussive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a binding prohibition, not a mere report that believers do not follow.
topics.reason: The following jussive verb selects the prohibitive function of the particle.

topics.headline: command comes before explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that authority leads and the conditional explanation follows.
topics.reason: The prohibition precedes the later whoever-condition in the ayah sequence.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII jussive plural following with explicit step-object
words.root_gloss_range: following, pursuing, tracing, and dependent alignment; local object selects stepwise adoption
words.prose: {{ar:تَتَّبِعُوا۟}} ({{tr:tattabiʿū}}) forbids the addressed believers from tracking a specific step-object, not from generic movement. Its jussive second-person plural form makes the command direct, while Form VIII gives the following a sense of adopted alignment; the same root will be echoed as a whoever-case later in the ayah.

topics.headline: following aimed at steps
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the forbidden following is not generic motion but tracking a marked step-object.
topics.reason: The verb takes the step noun as explicit object and the rows identify a constrained pair.

topics.headline: second-person binding prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the addressed believers themselves placed under a categorical negative command.
topics.reason: The second-person plural jussive matches the vocative audience under the prohibitive particle.

topics.headline: internalized pursuit in Form VIII
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses following as adopted alignment, while local context keeps the sense tied to the steps phrase rather than every dependence branch.
topics.reason: Form VIII supports internalized pursuit, but the object phrase narrows the active sense.

topics.headline: prohibition echoed as whoever-case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same following root move from direct you-command into a later whoever-condition.
topics.reason: The ayah repeats the same root and form in the conditional clause.

words.gloss_range: plural construct step-object attributed to the adversary
words.root_gloss_range: step, pace, and interval field; local plural metaphor makes deviation incremental
words.prose: {{ar:خُطُوَٰتِ}} ({{tr:khuṭuwāti}}) makes the danger concrete and procedural: steps, paces, and repeated increments become the thing followed. The construct relation sources those increments to the adversary, variant evidence adds pace-and-distance and acoustic weight without displacing the canonical phrase, and the rare marked formula recurs in warning settings (2:168; 2:208; 6:142). The heavy emphatic sound reinforces the physical thud of repeated steps.

topics.headline: adversary-sourced object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the steps as grammatically sourced to the adversary while the whole phrase functions as what is followed.
topics.reason: The noun is a construct head with the adversary as genitive complement and object role by phrase position.

topics.headline: plural footsteps make danger procedural
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures danger as repeated small steps that become a path, not only a single final sin.
topics.reason: The plural step noun and following verb jointly support an incremental-procedural image.

topics.headline: accepted step-variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a pace-and-distance nuance from the variant evidence, while the canonical local reading remains the plural steps phrase.
topics.reason: Variant evidence is useful contrast but does not replace the canonical local surface.

topics.headline: rare formula across legal domains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the expression as a marked recurring formula also found in legal or communal warning settings (2:168; 2:208; 6:142).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete parallels and rarity evidence for the formula.

topics.headline: emphatic sound weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the heavy consonantal cluster reinforce the weighted step image.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows add a sound-level payoff to the concrete step noun.

words.gloss_range: definite singular genitive adversary as source of the steps
words.root_gloss_range: remoteness and adversarial estrangement field; local noun names the concrete adversary
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāni}}) fixes the steps to one definite adversarial source. Etymological pressure of remoteness and estrangement colors the name, with burning or perishing as secondary destructive pressure, but the local noun remains concrete, not a paraphrase for abstract evil; the first mention also sets up the repeated genitive anchor of the next beat.

topics.headline: known adversary as genitive source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the plural steps traced to one definite adversarial source.
topics.reason: The definite singular genitive noun is the possessor-source of the construct phrase.

topics.headline: estrangement pressure in the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the adversary as marked by estrangement and remoteness, with burning or perishing as secondary destructive pressure, while the local word remains the definite adversary noun.
topics.reason: The etymological rows supply pressure without displacing the local concrete noun.

topics.headline: not abstract evil only
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not flatten the source into abstract evil; the phrase names a concrete adversarial commander field.
topics.reason: The noun tag and command collocation support a concrete adversary rather than abstraction.

topics.headline: first adversary beat before repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this first adversary mention sets up a repeated genitive anchor in the next beat.
topics.reason: The same phrase recurs in the conditional clause.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the explanatory conditional
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes the discourse into an explanatory condition. It links the prohibition to consequence, so the next clause does not merely add information but explains why the forbidden following matters.

topics.headline: conjunction opens explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah move from prohibition into an explanatory whoever-condition rather than simple addition.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the conditional clause that explains the prior command.

words.gloss_range: conditional pronoun generalizing the prohibited case
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens a whoever-condition governed by the following jussive. The warning moves from the addressed you to any human case, and the same surface form later helps reverse the ayah from human action to divine selection.

topics.headline: whoever-case under jussive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the warning generalized from the addressed you to any person who enters the condition.
topics.reason: The conditional pronoun governs the jussive verb and creates an open human variable.

topics.headline: surface reused for agency reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first man-form center human action before the later man-form centers divine selection.
topics.reason: The same surface later returns with a different clause function.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII singular jussive repeating the following action under condition
words.root_gloss_range: following and dependent adoption field; local verb converts the prohibition into a general conditional case
words.prose: {{ar:يَتَّبِعْ}} ({{tr:yattabiʿ}}) repeats the same following action inside the conditional frame. The form shifts from plural you to singular whoever, preserving the adopted-following sense while turning the command into a general case law.

topics.headline: following repeated under condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prohibited action converted into the condition that triggers the result.
topics.reason: The singular jussive verb follows the conditional pronoun and governs the same object type.

topics.headline: same adopted-following form returns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same Form VIII pursuit in a singular whoever-case, while the local grammar limits it to the conditional frame.
topics.reason: The form repeats word 6 under conditional mood.

topics.headline: you-command becomes whoever-case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rhetorical echo shift from communal command to individualizing case law.
topics.reason: The row family explicitly links this verb to the earlier plural prohibition.

words.gloss_range: repeated plural construct step-object in the conditional protasis
words.root_gloss_range: step and pace field; local repetition carries the same procedural danger into the explanation
words.prose: {{ar:خُطُوَٰتِ}} ({{tr:khuṭuwāti}}) repeats the exact step-object in the condition, so the explanation stays locked to the original prohibition. The second occurrence keeps the route-image active and binds beat one and beat two in parallel.

topics.headline: same sourced object in condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the condition repeat the same adversary-sourced step-object rather than introducing a new danger.
topics.reason: The repeated construct phrase remains the object of following in the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: condition as traversed route
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the explanatory condition as a route being traversed step by step.
topics.reason: The same step image is carried into the conditional consequence frame.

topics.headline: beat-one and beat-two parallelism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exact phrase repetition tying the direct prohibition to the general condition.
topics.reason: The phrase repeats across the first two beats of the ayah.

words.gloss_range: second definite genitive adversary closing the repeated object phrase
words.root_gloss_range: adversarial remoteness field; local repeat stabilizes the antecedent for the result clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-shayṭāni}}) restates the estranged adversary-source at the end of the repeated object phrase. That repetition fixes the antecedent field before the result pronoun and binds the prohibition and conditional explanation to the same source.

topics.headline: second genitive adversary source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the estranged adversary-source restated just before the result clause, leaving the referent fixed.
topics.reason: The second definite singular genitive repeats the source relation and stabilizes identity.

topics.headline: antecedent prepared for result pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated adversary phrase prepares the following pronoun and result.
topics.reason: The word closes the repeated object phrase immediately before the emphatic result.

topics.headline: same genitive anchor in both beats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same adversary anchor bind the prohibition and the conditional explanation.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly track the phrase repetition.

words.gloss_range: answer particle introducing the conditional result
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) marks the answer to the condition. The result follows immediately from the whoever-case and pivots into an emphatic assertion.

topics.headline: answer particle for the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the result arrive as the immediate answer to the whoever-condition.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the conditional apodosis and pivots into the emphatic result.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle opening the asserted result clause with attached-pronoun force
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) gives the conditional result assertive force. Its attached-pronoun bridge carries attention from following the steps to the commanding agent, while the antecedent chain remains compact enough to preserve the ayah's agency risk.

topics.headline: asserted result after condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the consequence stated with assertion, not left as a tentative inference.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle governs the nominal result clause after the answer particle.

topics.headline: compact pronoun bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pronoun bridge transfers attention from following the steps to the agent that commands, while antecedent ambiguity cautions against over-specifying beyond the local chain.
topics.reason: The fused pronoun links the condition to the command verb, but the rows themselves flag antecedent complexity.

words.gloss_range: indicative command verb selecting its content through the following preposition
words.root_gloss_range: command, affair, and authority field; local verb presents the adversary as issuing commands
words.prose: {{ar:يَأْمُرُ}} ({{tr:yaʾmuru}}) exposes what following the steps leads to: the adversary becomes a commander issuing specific ethical content. The verb's authority field matters here, and the pattern of adversary-command has concrete parallels at (2:169) and (2:268).

topics.headline: adversary commands as ongoing predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the adversary not only leaving steps but actively issuing commands as an ongoing pattern.
topics.reason: The indicative Form I verb functions inside the emphatic result clause.

topics.headline: command takes explicit content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an authority relation: the one followed becomes the one commanding specific content.
topics.reason: The verb selects its commanded content through the following prepositional phrase.

topics.headline: adversary-command formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a Quranic pattern in which the adversary commands indecency, with parallels at (2:169) and (2:268).
topics.reason: The rows identify a concrete formulaic field for the command verb and ethical content.

words.gloss_range: preposition making the commanded content explicit
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) turns the following ethical nouns into the content of the command. A single preposition holds both nouns under the same command relation, so the pair is one governed object-field.

topics.headline: preposition specifies commanded content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command’s object-content made explicit rather than the preposition being merely instrumental.
topics.reason: The preposition attaches the command relation to the following ethical noun.

topics.headline: one preposition governs the dyad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both ethical nouns are held under one command relation.
topics.reason: The single preposition governs the paired noun phrase through coordination.

words.gloss_range: definite abstract noun for recognized boundary-violating indecency
words.root_gloss_range: excess, enormity, and boundary-violation field; local noun is broader than only sexual misconduct
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ}} ({{tr:al-faḥshāʾi}}) names a recognized category of boundary-violating excess under that command. Its abstract intensive form makes the violation category-level, not merely one act, and the dyad is familiar in ethical discourse (3:104; 16:90; 29:45), with a same-surah link to the slander field (24:19).

topics.headline: definite governed ethical category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a recognized category of wrongdoing made the content of the command.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and genitive after the preposition.

topics.headline: excess beyond proper bounds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the term as boundary-violating excess, not only sexual misconduct, while the local dyad keeps it within ethical command content.
topics.reason: The root rows broaden the semantic range, but the local pairing supplies the ethical frame.

topics.headline: abstract intensified quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a quality-category of violation rather than one isolated act.
topics.reason: The abstract noun tag and pattern rows support category-level force.

topics.headline: paired with the rejectable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a familiar ethical dyad with parallels at (3:104), (16:90), and (29:45), and a same-surah link to the slander field (24:19).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete pair parallels and a same-surah echo.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining the two ethical nouns under one command relation
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second ethical noun under the same prepositional governance. The command content widens into two axes without turning the second into a mere gloss of the first.

topics.headline: second noun added under same governance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command content widen into two coordinated ethical axes without making the second a mere apposition.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the two governed nouns in one content phrase.

words.gloss_range: definite passive-participle ethical noun coordinated with indecency
words.root_gloss_range: unknown, denied, rejected, and morally disapproved field; local noun names what is recognized as rejectable
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُنكَرِ}} ({{tr:al-munkari}}) completes the pair as a definite passive-participle ethical noun. The word carries rejection and non-recognition pressure while the local sense names what is morally rejectable; punishment-related root pressure stays secondary, and the ethical opposition is visible in parallels such as (47:6) and (3:104).

topics.headline: definite rejectable category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second noun share the same governance while naming a recognized category of what is rejected.
topics.reason: The coordinated passive-participle noun remains genitive under the prepositional command content.

topics.headline: rejection and non-recognition pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses wrongdoing as something cognition and conscience reject, while the local noun remains an ethical category rather than naming a rejecting subject.
topics.reason: The passive-participle form leaves the rejecting subject open but licenses the rejection field.

topics.headline: punishment branch as consequence pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels consequence pressure from the wider root field, while local grammar selects moral disapproval rather than a punishment noun.
topics.reason: The punishment-related rows are valid root pressure but not the selected local lexical sense.

topics.headline: paired ethical discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the term’s ethical pairing field, including contrast with the recognized-good root at (47:6) and (3:104).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete discourse pairings and opposition evidence.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction pivoting from warning to counterfactual dependence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from warning and consequence into counterfactual dependence. A new logical phase begins: what prevents the entire failure just described.

topics.headline: warning pivots to grace-dependence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a new phase: after the command and consequence, the ayah turns to what prevents total failure.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the counterfactual clause and marks a discourse pivot.

words.gloss_range: counterfactual prevention particle with explicit negative answer
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) frames the next nouns as the preventing condition. Because that protasis exists, the later negated answer states what would otherwise have happened: no purification at all.

topics.headline: prevention frame with negative answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clause as prevention because grace and mercy are present; without them, the negative result would stand.
topics.reason: The particle takes a nominative protasis and is answered by the later negated purification clause.

words.gloss_range: nominative construct favor as first counterfactual support
words.root_gloss_range: surplus, excellence, bounty, and excess-beyond-owed field; local noun marks unearned preventive favor
words.prose: {{ar:فَضْلُ}} ({{tr:faḍlu}}) is the first support named in the prevention frame. As construct favor it receives divine specificity, and the root's surplus-beyond-owed pressure makes the rescue feel like an unearned protective margin; the favor-mercy pair has concrete parallels (2:64; 4:83; 24:14).

topics.headline: favor as counterfactual support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine favor functioning as a causal support in the prevention frame.
topics.reason: The nominative construct noun is the first subject in the counterfactual protasis.

topics.headline: unearned surplus beyond what is owed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses favor as surplus beyond entitlement and as a protective margin, while local syntax keeps it as the named preventive resource.
topics.reason: The root rows support surplus pressure but the local construct selects divine favor.

topics.headline: paired rescue terms
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes favor and mercy as paired rescue terms, with parallels at (2:64), (4:83), and (24:14).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete pair parallels and a boundary reprise in the surah.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name specifying the source of favor
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field; local genitive marks source, not a generic deity category
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) supplies the source of that favor as the named divine referent. Need-and-bewilderment derivational pressure remains secondary to the proper-name function, while this genitive occurrence begins a three-case divine-name structure: source of favor, agent of purification, and final subject of hearing and knowledge; the lawla formula also recalls (24:14).

topics.headline: divine name sources favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees favor tied to the named divine source, not left as an abstract resource.
topics.reason: The proper noun is genitive as the complement of the favor construct.

topics.headline: need and bewilderment pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses need-and-bewilderment pressure around the divine name, while local grammar keeps it as a proper genitive source.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute can color the name but cannot replace the proper-name function.

topics.headline: first of three divine-name cases
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first divine-name case in a sequence that maps source, agent, and final subject, with a same-surah lawla reprise at (24:14).
topics.reason: The rows track the divine name across genitive, accusative, and nominative roles and give a concrete same-surah parallel.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus second-person plural suffix placing favor upon the audience
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) places the favor upon the addressed group. After the generic whoever-case, the second-person suffix returns the rescue frame to the same community summoned at the beginning.

topics.headline: favor placed over the addressed group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rescue frame return directly to the addressed community through the suffix.
topics.reason: The preposition plus plural suffix binds the counterfactual support to the audience.

topics.headline: you-thread after whoever-case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah return from the generic whoever-case to the same addressed you.
topics.reason: The second-person suffix resumes the addressee thread after the third-person conditional.

words.gloss_range: conjunction coordinating mercy with favor inside the counterfactual frame
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates mercy with favor inside the same counterfactual protasis. The ayah's prevention frame rests on paired support rather than on a single isolated term.

topics.headline: mercy coordinated with favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the counterfactual prevention rest on a paired support frame, not favor alone.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the second support noun with the first inside the same protasis.

words.gloss_range: nominative mercy noun with suffix returning it to God
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, compassion, and womb-related care field; local noun names deployed divine mercy
words.prose: {{ar:رَحْمَتُهُۥ}} ({{tr:raḥmatuhū}}) completes the paired support frame, with the suffix returning mercy to God. The root's womb-compassion pressure survives as protective care, but locally mercy functions as the last named preventive resource before the ayah states that no one would have become purified without it.

topics.headline: mercy belongs to God in the lawla frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mercy as a second nominative support that is explicitly returned to God by suffix.
topics.reason: The noun is coordinated as a subject in the counterfactual protasis and carries the divine-referent suffix.

topics.headline: compassionate-care pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses mercy as womb-related protective compassion, while local syntax keeps it paired with favor as a preventive resource.
topics.reason: The root image contributes semantic pressure but does not override the local support-frame role.

topics.headline: last named preventive condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mercy as the final named condition before the clause says no one would have become purified.
topics.reason: The noun completes the favor-mercy protasis immediately before the negative apodosis.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening the counterfactual answer
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the counterfactual answer by negating the purification verb. Its force will be stretched by the later no-one and never terms into a total impossibility claim.

topics.headline: counterfactual answer negates purification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the counterfactual answer begin as negation of purification, not as a relative clause.
topics.reason: The particle negates the following perfect verb in the lawla answer.

topics.headline: negation bracketed to total impossibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the negation will be stretched to total impossibility by the later never-word.
topics.reason: The rows identify the bracketing construction from the negative particle to the final adverb.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect purification/growth verb under counterfactual negation
words.root_gloss_range: growth and purity field; local Form I marks unaided purification as impossible under the counterfactual
words.prose: {{ar:زَكَىٰ}} ({{tr:zakā}}) names purification or growth as the impossible result under the counterfactual negation. The growth-purity root field keeps purification developmental, and the Form I verb is crucial: what no one would achieve unaided is later answered by God's Form II caused purification, while the transitive variant remains contrastive. Related purification language appears at (53:32), (91:9), (4:49), and (24:28).

topics.headline: Form I purification under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees unaided purification or growth placed under the impossible counterfactual.
topics.reason: The Form I perfect verb is negated in the counterfactual answer and contrasted with the later Form II.

topics.headline: growth and purity converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses purification as developmental growth as well as cleansing.
topics.reason: The root rows support both growth and purity in the local purification field.

topics.headline: Form I contrasted with caused purification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the theology carried by the form shift: impossible self-purification is answered by caused divine purification, while the transitive variant remains contrastive.
topics.reason: The canonical local verb is Form I, and the later Form II supplies the active contrast.

topics.headline: root returns in social ethics
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the purification root belong to a larger discourse, with related contrasts at (53:32), (91:9), (4:49), and later social-ethics wording in this surah (24:28).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete purification parallels and same-surah forward pressure.

words.gloss_range: partitive preposition plus audience suffix marking the population under negation
words.prose: {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) locates the zero-case inside the addressed community. The same you who receive favor are also the population from whom no purified individual would emerge without it.

topics.headline: from among you as zero-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the impossible purification scoped within the addressed community itself.
topics.reason: The partitive phrase marks the population from which no purified person would emerge.

topics.headline: same you held across clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressees receiving favor are the same community named inside the negated purification claim.
topics.reason: The second-person pronouns tie the grace frame and negation frame to one group.

words.gloss_range: emphatic preposition under negation before the indefinite individual
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) intensifies the negation before the indefinite individual. Under negation it pushes the claim down to the smallest possible member: not even one.

topics.headline: extra preposition exhausts the minimum
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the negation intensified down to even a single individual.
topics.reason: The preposition under negation functions emphatically before the indefinite individual.

words.gloss_range: indefinite singular under negation universalizing no one at all
words.root_gloss_range: oneness and singularity field; local indefinite atomizes the negated group
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدٍ}} ({{tr:aḥadin}}) atomizes the community under negation. Its singularity pressure makes the counterfactual exhaustive, while the famous oneness use at (112:1) remains lexical contrast rather than the selected local sense.

topics.headline: indefinite singular universalizes negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the group atomized: not one individual would escape the counterfactual failure.
topics.reason: The indefinite singular noun under negation universalizes the scope.

topics.headline: absolute one-pressure as lexical contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses singularity pressure, with the famous oneness use at (112:1) serving as lexical contrast rather than the local theological sense.
topics.reason: The row supplies a concrete reference, but local syntax selects the indefinite no-one function.

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal adverb sealing the negation as never
words.root_gloss_range: perpetuity and duration field; local adverb extends the counterfactual negation indefinitely
words.prose: {{ar:أَبَدًۭا}} ({{tr:abadan}}) seals the counterfactual as temporal never. Together with the negation, partitives, and single-person scope, it turns the clause into maximal impossibility: no one among you, ever.

topics.headline: adverbial never seals the clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the counterfactual negation extended indefinitely: no one, ever.
topics.reason: The accusative temporal adverb closes and intensifies the negated clause.

topics.headline: maximal negation stack
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the full stack of negation, partitives, single-person scope, and never-time working together.
topics.reason: The row explicitly names the combined negation structure.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening the adversative correction
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the adversative turn. The ayah moves from incapacity into the divine agency that corrects it.

topics.headline: pivot from incapacity to agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah turn from total human incapacity toward the divine agency that remedies it.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the corrective particle and begins the next logical phase.

words.gloss_range: corrective emphatic particle governing the divine name
words.prose: {{ar:لَٰكِنَّ}} ({{tr:lākinna}}) prevents the prior negation from becoming despair. It introduces the correction: purification is impossible as unaided human achievement, but not impossible as divine action.

topics.headline: correction after despairing negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the severe negation corrected, not left as despair: the remedy is divine purification.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following divine name and pairs structurally with the earlier counterfactual frame.

words.gloss_range: accusative divine name as subject of the corrective particle
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field; local accusative marks the agent of the corrective purification clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:allāha}}) is the accusative subject of the corrective particle and the agent who answers the impossibility. It is the middle divine-name case, shifting from source of favor to active purifier before the final nominative attribute subject.

topics.headline: divine name as corrective agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees God reintroduced as the agent who answers the impossibility just stated.
topics.reason: The divine name is accusative as the subject of the corrective particle.

topics.headline: middle divine-name case marks agency pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the middle appearance of the divine name shift from source-of-favor to active purifier before the final attribute subject.
topics.reason: The rows track the three syntactic cases of the divine name in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: Form II indicative purification verb with an open human object
words.root_gloss_range: growth, purity, and productive increase field; local Form II makes purification divinely caused
words.prose: {{ar:يُزَكِّى}} ({{tr:yuzakkī}}) states the corrective action as ongoing divine purification of an open object. Growth and bestowed increase color the root as productive cultivation rather than mere subtraction of fault, but the visible Form II doubling is the central payoff: what no one would realize in Form I is caused by God here, in a formula echoed at (4:49) and (53:32).

topics.headline: ongoing divine action with open object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees purification asserted as ongoing divine action directed toward an open human object.
topics.reason: The indicative verb takes the following relative pronoun as direct object in the corrective clause.

topics.headline: growth and productive giving pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses purification as productive growth and bestowed increase, not mere subtraction of fault, while local grammar selects divine purification as the active sense.
topics.reason: The root and noun-field rows supply pressure without replacing the local verb sense.

topics.headline: caused purification contrasts Form I failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the visible Form II doubling and form shift: what no one would achieve in Form I is caused by God in Form II.
topics.reason: The doubled morphology marks the causative/intensive Form II and directly contrasts the earlier Form I verb.

topics.headline: divine purification formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the clause as part of a divine purification formula also heard at (4:49) and (53:32), with forward social-ethics pressure in this surah.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete parallels and same-surah forward linkage.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun as the object of divine purification
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) leaves the purified recipient open as the object of divine purification. The repeated man-form reverses the ayah's agency pattern: first whoever follows, now whom God wills.

topics.headline: open object of divine purification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the purified recipient left open rather than named or claimed by default.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun functions as the direct object of the purification verb.

topics.headline: same form reverses agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated man-form invert the ayah from whoever follows to whom God wills.
topics.reason: The same form appears first as conditional human agency and here as relative object of divine selection.

words.gloss_range: Form I imperfect divine willing completing the open object phrase
words.root_gloss_range: willing, choosing, determining, and thinghood field; local verb makes divine will the criterion for purification
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) completes the open object phrase by making divine will the criterion. The criteria are not stated, the will is ongoing and direct, and determinate-selection pressure survives without turning the local clause into a broad ontology of thinghood; the verb lands the corrective clause just before the attribute seal.

topics.headline: will leaves criteria unstated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the criteria for purification left undisclosed: whom He wills is not further specified.
topics.reason: The verb has no explicit object beyond its relation to the relative pronoun.

topics.headline: ongoing direct divine volition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears divine willing as a live, direct criterion for purification rather than a past or mediated process.
topics.reason: The imperfect indicative Form I verb belongs to the local purification-selection field.

topics.headline: will as determinate selection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses will as determinate choosing that makes the selected purification effective, while the local clause does not require a broad ontology of thinghood.
topics.reason: The root-family rows support determinate will and thinghood pressure, but local syntax selects the will criterion.

topics.headline: will closes before attribute seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the corrective purification clause land on divine will just before the final hearing-and-knowing seal.
topics.reason: The word closes the object phrase and the corrective clause before the final nominal sentence.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening the closing nominal attribute sentence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes into the final nominal sentence. After condition, counterfactual, and correction, this fourth pivot moves from action and will to the attributes that ground the whole warning.

topics.headline: conjunction opens final seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a shift from what God does and wills into the attributes that ground the whole warning.
topics.reason: The conjunction opens a new nominal predicative seal after the will clause.

topics.headline: fourth logical phase marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this as the fourth conjunction pivot after condition, counterfactual, and correction.
topics.reason: The rows identify four conjunction-initiated phases in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine name as subject of the final attributes
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field; local nominative unifies the actor of favor, purification, hearing, and knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) stands as the subject of the final attribute clause. The nominal closure asserts stable attributes, and the repeated divine name now unifies source of favor, agent of purification, and subject of hearing and knowledge.

topics.headline: divine name subject of attributes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final clause assert stable divine attributes rather than narrate one more event.
topics.reason: The nominative proper noun is the subject of the final nominal sentence and supports two predicates.

topics.headline: source, agent, and knower unified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same divine name move through source of favor, agent of purification, and subject of hearing and knowledge.
topics.reason: The rows track the three case roles and their theological structure.

words.gloss_range: first indefinite predicate in the final attribute pair
words.root_gloss_range: hearing, listening, and responsive reception field; local form marks stable comprehensive hearing
words.prose: {{ar:سَمِيعٌ}} ({{tr:samīʿun}}) is the first predicate of the closing seal. In an ayah filled with address, command, and response, hearing comes first as stable comprehensive reception, not momentary active-participle hearing; the familiar hearing-knowing pair appears in examples such as (2:127), (2:137), and (2:181), and it also answers the human hearing tested earlier in the surah (24:12).

topics.headline: hearing as first predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears divine hearing placed first in the closing pair, answering a verse full of address, command, and response.
topics.reason: The word is the first predicate of the final nominal sentence and precedes knowledge.

topics.headline: stable responsive hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses not momentary active-participle hearing but comprehensive, stable reception of the command discourse.
topics.reason: The root family and faʿīl pattern support stable responsive hearing.

topics.headline: frequent hearing-knowing pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a familiar attribute pair, with examples at (2:127), (2:137), and (2:181), grounding divine selection in perception.
topics.reason: The rows identify the recurring pair and its local position after the will clause.

topics.headline: human hearing answered by divine hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees same-surah hearing language return after human hearing was ethically tested in the slander episode (24:12).
topics.reason: The echo rows give a concrete same-surah reference and forward resonance.

words.gloss_range: second indefinite predicate completing the final attribute pair
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, awareness, and comprehensive cognition field; local form marks complete knowledge of hidden states
words.prose: {{ar:عَلِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) completes the final pair as the second predicate of the same divine subject. Its comprehensive knowledge covers the hidden criteria left unstated by whom He wills, and the matched intensive form joins hearing and knowledge so inscrutable selection does not read as arbitrariness or ignorance.

topics.headline: knowledge completes double predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one divine subject receive both predicates, joining hearing and knowledge in the closure.
topics.reason: The word is the second predicate in the final nominal sentence.

topics.headline: comprehensive knowledge of hidden criteria
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the unstated criteria of whom God wills placed under complete knowledge rather than ignorance.
topics.reason: The root rows and local will-selection context support knowledge beyond observable speech.

topics.headline: matched intensive attribute pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the matched forms create a balanced seal of complete audition and complete cognition.
topics.reason: The faʿīl pattern parallels the prior predicate and the co-occurrence rows identify the pair.

topics.headline: selection closed by complete awareness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees open divine will followed by complete awareness, so inscrutability does not read as arbitrariness or ignorance.
topics.reason: The final attribute pair immediately follows the will-selection clause and grounds it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled construction تَتَّبِعُوا/يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَاتِ makes following discrete traces the repeated action, while ش ط ن supplies distance and rupture.
baseline_models.mechanism: A walker does not arrive at فحشاء and منكر in one leap. Tracing one footprint after another creates path dependence: each bounded step makes the next available, progressively crossing limits and carrying the walker into estrangement and moral unrecognizability.

activation_trace.role: Following as tracing one mark after another supplies the incremental path mechanism.
The span between two feet makes each movement a bounded, repeatable unit.
Distance and severance provide the path's cumulative direction away from secure relation.
Exceeding a limit identifies the threshold-crossing outcome of accumulated steps.
Change into something unknown or disapproved marks the end state as a deformation of recognition.

changed_reading.before: The verse forbids isolated acts of obedience to Satan because they lead to major sins.
changed_reading.after: The verse diagnoses incremental path formation: small trace-following decisions progressively cross limits, create distance, and make the resulting conduct morally unrecognizable.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يَتَّبِعْ, يَأْمُرُ, and their consequences join following, command, and outcome in one conditional chain.
baseline_models.mechanism: Repeated compliance lets an alien command acquire practical authority. The long-cord image in ش ط ن and the attached liability in ت ب ع make the sequence resemble a tether: following both binds the follower to the commanding source and leaves a consequence attached to the follower.

activation_trace.role: An attached claim or consequence turns following into liability rather than neutral imitation.
The long, tightly twisted cord supplies a material image for cumulative attachment to a remote source.
Demand and obligation make the source more than a suggester: it behaves as a rival commander.
The opposite of recognition characterizes what this rival authority normalizes.

changed_reading.before: Satan offers temptations that an individual may accept or reject.
changed_reading.after: Each compliance helps install a rival command relation: the follower becomes tethered to its demands and acquires the liability that follows them.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The exhaustive مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا is reversed by وَلَكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزَكِّى, shifting purification's effective agent.
baseline_models.mechanism: فضل and رحمة are not merely rewards after self-purification. Gifted surplus and tender care are the prior medium in which purification can occur; ز ك و holds removal of corruption together with positive growth, while the negative construction excludes every person and every duration from self-sufficiency.

activation_trace.role: Gift and benefaction supply the enabling provision that the counterfactual says cannot be omitted.
Tender mercy supplies a sustaining relation rather than a merely forensic cancellation.
Growth and increase make purification a positive development, not only removal.
Purity and soundness retain the cleansing dimension within that growth.
Exhaustive negation blocks every individual exception to dependence on grace.
Duration and permanence extend that blocked self-sufficiency across time.

changed_reading.before: Divine grace forgives a person after the person resists or falls into sin.
changed_reading.after: Divine gift and mercy are the prior productive condition for any cleansing growth at all; purification cannot be extracted from the isolated self.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier speech sequence converts plural footsteps into a relay. A truth-diverted claim is held by a mutually supporting group, received at the tongue, and diffused among believers; each reception and retransmission is a small followable trace, and each participant acquires a share of the resulting liability.

activation_trace.role: Trace-by-trace following provides the focus mechanism that the speech relay concretizes.
A path made of visible traces lets each transmitted item become the next person's cue.
A lie diverted from truth supplies the distorted object passed along the path.
A surrounding, mutually supporting group turns an individual path into a transmission network.
Acquisition assigns each relay participant a personally gained share of the wrongdoing.
Receiving speech by taking it up and prompting it names the handoff between relay nodes.
Diffusion and spreading describe the network-scale result of repeated handoffs.
Manifest ugliness is the same focus outcome now shown spreading through a community.

structural_cues: 24:11 places a surrounding group beside the statement that each person acquired a share.
24:12-16 repeat hearing, saying, tongues, mouths, and lack of knowledge before 24:19 names social spread.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a group, individual acquisition, tongue-level reception, and diffusion; I supply the arrow that treats each speech handoff as one of the focus's plural steps. The live alternative is that خُطُوَات remains broader than rumor even though rumor is a concrete instance.

changed_reading.before: The steps form an individual's private progression toward obscenity.
changed_reading.after: The steps can be socially distributed: receiving and repeating an unverified claim leaves a trace for the next speaker, spreads obscenity, and allocates liability across the relay.

context_deltas.mechanism: The فضل and رحمة that make purification possible are immediately given a social outlet. People possessing surplus and capacity continue giving, erase the offense's trace, turn from retaliation beautifully, and seek divine covering; grace therefore interrupts the harmful sequence by being relayed rather than hoarded.

activation_trace.role: Divine benefaction is the focus's enabling source.
Tender mercy keeps the enabling source relational.
Growth identifies what the received grace is meant to produce.
Benefaction now characterizes human holders who can pass provision onward.
Material breadth supplies practical capacity for continued giving.
Erasure of a trace models refusal to preserve the offense as the next retaliatory step.
Beautifully turning aside from the offense gives the counter-path a social action.
Covering fault and protecting its bearer makes divine forgiveness the desired pattern and destination.
The returning mercy closes the relay at the same source named in the focus.

structural_cues: 24:20 repeats فضل and رحمة immediately before the focus, and 24:22 moves from possessors of فضل and سعة to giving, pardon, and turning the page.
24:22 motivates human pardon by asking whether its hearers desire God's forgiveness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated grace language and a sequence from possessed surplus to pardon and desired forgiveness; I infer that received grace is meant to circulate as a counter-sequence. The alternative is that 24:22 is an adjacent injunction rather than an enacted form of the focus's purification.

changed_reading.before: Purification depends on a divine gift received by an otherwise incapable individual.
changed_reading.after: The gift remains divine in origin but becomes socially active: its recipient interrupts retaliation through continued giving, trace-erasure, and pardon, allowing grace to generate further purification.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later uses of أزكى place purification at the first controllable boundary: before entry, permission is required and refusal triggers return; before desire develops, sight is reduced and vulnerable openings are guarded. These are practical brakes on the earliest step rather than repairs after arrival.

activation_trace.role: Crossing or overstepping supplies the boundary dimension latent in each step.
Purity is the focus outcome that the later boundary practices concretize.
Entering an interior supplies a literal threshold where movement can be stopped.
Permission makes crossing dependent on another person's authorized boundary.
Returning supplies a reversible counter-movement when entry is refused.
The text explicitly marks that return at the threshold as purer.
Reducing and restraining input places a brake at the visual intake stage.
Eyesight identifies the sensory gate being regulated.
Guarding sanctity and chastity gives sustained protection to the vulnerable boundary.
An open place of vulnerability supplies the guarded opening in the mechanism.
The repeated purity judgment links sensory restraint to the same focus outcome.

structural_cues: 24:27-28 conditions movement into another household on recognition, greeting, and permission, then calls returning أزكى.
24:30 moves from lowered sight to guarded openings and again calls the practice أزكى.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two explicit أزكى judgments attached to entry and sensory boundaries; I infer that they are concrete anti-step controls for 24:21. The alternative is that the repeated root marks independent etiquettes without specifying the mechanism of Satanic following.

changed_reading.before: Avoiding Satan's steps means resisting a temptation once its moral content is apparent.
changed_reading.after: Purity is protected upstream by governing thresholds, permissions, attention, and openings, with immediate return functioning as a positive counter-step.

context_deltas.mechanism: The whole-surah recurrence materializes ز ك و as a circulation of increase: people give zakāt, God increases them from فضل, and giving zakāt with responsive obedience opens toward mercy. The purification of 24:21 can therefore include an outward release of value that prevents growth from becoming self-enclosed.

activation_trace.role: Growth and increase provide the focus sense that later giving makes materially visible.
Surplus and remainder supply the excess from which the growth cycle operates.
The shared root places named giving inside the branch image of growth and increase.
Explicit increase supplies the return movement in the circulation.
Increase coming from surplus reconnects the cycle to the focus's فضل.
The command to give zakāt makes growth an enacted communal practice.
Responsive obedience supplies the willing movement that carries the practice.
Mercy is the relational horizon toward which giving and obedience move.

structural_cues: 24:37 names giving zakāt, 24:38 immediately answers faithful work with increase from فضل, and 24:56 joins zakāt and obedience to hoped-for mercy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated ز ك و, explicit increase from فضل, and mercy after giving; I infer a circulation model linking inner purification to outward release. The live alternative is that zakāt and يُزَكِّي activate distinct senses of the root and should not be functionally fused.

changed_reading.before: God's purification is chiefly an inward cleansing of an individual.
changed_reading.after: One material expression of divinely sourced growth may be outward circulation: value is released through zakāt, answered by increase from فضل, and held within mercy.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later obedience sequence supplies a rival path architecture. Satan commands what is منكر, contrary to recognition; faithful response is hearing joined to obedience and طاعة معروفة, recognized good. Legitimate command leads toward guidance and explicit burdens, whereas resistance appears as covert slipping away, concealment behind others, and taking a different path.

activation_trace.role: Demand and obligation establish the focus's rival command source.
Contrariety to recognition marks the quality produced by that command.
Divine hearing places all spoken commands and responses within an audited field.
Hearing as understanding and compliance turns reception into a deliberate response.
Willing submission supplies the alternative following relation.
The repeated command root makes the source-of-command contrast explicit.
Obedience names the movement expected on the legitimate path.
Recognized good directly reverses the focus's unrecognized or disapproved outcome.
Entrusted burden makes responsibility explicit rather than leaving a hidden attached liability.
Gentle direction to a path gives obedience a stated destination.
Slipping out supplies a covert counter-movement away from the collective command.
Hiding behind another person describes how the evasive path masks itself.
Taking a path different from another's gives مخالفة a spatial path image.

structural_cues: 24:47 contrasts a claim of faith and obedience with subsequent turning away; 24:51 gives the response سمعنا وأطعنا.
24:53 places command beside طاعة معروفة, while 24:63 places covert departure and concealment beside مخالفة عن أمره.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the منكر/معروفة reversal, hearing-obedience, guidance, assigned burdens, and covert departure from command; I infer that 24:21 concerns authentication between rival command paths, not only appetite. The alternative is that the later passages regulate public authority without defining Satanic influence.

changed_reading.before: The command in 24:21 is a generic metaphor for temptation.
changed_reading.after: The verse contrasts rival regimes of response: one normalizes what defeats recognition and attaches hidden liability, while the other is heard, recognized as good, responsibility-bearing, and path-guiding.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because 24:31 juxtaposes a follower category with feet making hidden adornment knowable; it does not equate those referents with Satan or redefine that ayah's rules. It remains anchored to the focus's following and footsteps as a mechanism of trace production, and downstream prose should present it only as an information-channel analogy.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: In 24:21 a person follows preexisting footsteps; 24:31 activates the inverse possibility that bodily movement itself emits a cue another person can register.

activation_trace.role: Following behind another supplies the receiver side of a trace channel.
Footsteps as traces supply the signal that can remain available to a follower.
The follower category keeps the relation of one person moving after another active in the context.
The bundled leg and foot occurrence grounds the explicit bodily source of the revealing cue.
Removal of concealment supplies the informational effect produced by the movement.
Something becoming known completes the movement-to-information channel.

changed_reading.before: Satan supplies a silent path and the human only walks it.
changed_reading.after: A walker may also emit socially legible traces; one person's small movement can disclose what was hidden and become another person's next followable cue.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain move from linear walking to optical layering, so it should not be stated as a lexical definition of خُطُوَات. It remains valid as a material analogy because the focus supplies repeated increments and growing distance, while 24:35 and 24:40 supply illumination versus covering; downstream prose should retain explicit analogical qualification.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The plural steps and the distancing branch of ش ط ن permit a cumulative model in which each movement reduces access to orientation.

activation_trace.role: Bounded repeated steps supply discrete units that can accumulate.
Increasing distance and severance supply the loss of orientation produced by accumulation.
Illumination supplies the counter-medium in which a path becomes visible.
A cover rising over something supplies one layer of cumulative occlusion.
The second mapped covering branch preserves the same occurrence's alternate inventory and reinforces concealment.
The stated absence of illumination supplies the terminal condition of lost visibility.

changed_reading.before: Each step advances horizontally toward a bad destination.
changed_reading.after: Each step may also add a covering layer that makes the path harder to see, while divinely given illumination functions as restored navigability.

strongest_changes: The rumor sequence makes footsteps distributed speech events: each reception and repetition leaves the next trace and assigns a share of liability.
The grace refrain becomes a social counter-sequence in 24:22, where possessed فضل is relayed through giving, trace-erasure, and pardon.
Repeated أزكى judgments move purification upstream into permission, return, visual restraint, and guarded openings.
منكر is reversed by طاعة معروفة, sharpening the verse into a contrast between rival command paths and their modes of response.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence turned 24:21 from a general warning into a process map: traces can be spoken, spatial, sensory, distributive, or institutional, while فضل and رحمة generate counter-movements rather than only repairing a completed fall.
remaining_uncertainties: The social relay from divine فضل to human pardon is strongly sequenced but remains a reader-supplied causal arrow.
The zakāt occurrences may activate a materially distinct sense from God's act of يُزَكِّي, so the circulation model should remain secondary.
The foot-signal and layered-occlusion readings are anchored analogies, not lexical equations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Corruption is modeled as path dependence assembled from small traces.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ت ب ع` B003 is stepwise tracking and B006 an incurred consequence; `خ ط و` B001 is a step/stride-space and B002 traces that are followed; `ز ك و` B001 is growth and B002 purification; `ف ح ش` B002 is exceeding a bound and `ن ك ر` B006 a condemned act requiring correction. **Structural cue:** 24:16-19 decompose rumor into utterance, recurrence, clarification, attachment, and spread; 24:22 supplies the alternative sequence of giving, pardoning, and turning a broad side away. **Assigned role:** each step is a locally small transition that accumulates into an ordered route, while purification is counter-growth that breaks the route. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies discrete traces and a resulting command; I infer repeated micro-compliance → path lock-in → bound-crossing conduct. **Reading change:** the warning concerns incremental process, not only an abrupt final temptation.

2. **The followed path can become a tether.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ش ط ن` B002 is a long twisted rope used for drawing or restraint, alongside B004's rebellious being; the doubled `خطوات الشيطان` supplies repeated attachment points. **Structural cue:** the two occurrences of following frame a causal statement, and 24:17 has already linked recurrence to habit. **Assigned role:** the rope image explains how individually chosen steps can accumulate into reduced freedom: each followed trace adds another turn to the tether. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies rope, steps, repetition, and command; I infer steps → twisted continuity → restraint by the route one has followed. This is exploratory because the rope image is dormant rather than demanded by the surface construction. **Reading change:** “following Satan” becomes self-binding through accumulated motion as well as obedience to an external commander.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:22's pardon and 24:26's clearance revealed a genuine counter-path to the tether: traces can be effaced, claims released, and protective covering restored.

baseline.text: Ey inananlar! Şeytanın adımlarını izlemeyin. Kim şeytanın adımlarını izlerse bilsin ki o, hayasızlığı ve kötülüğü emreder. Allah'ın size lütfu ve merhameti olmasaydı içinizden hiç kimse asla arınamazdı. Fakat Allah dilediğini arındırır. Allah işiten ve bilendir.

findings.text: Bozulma bir anda değil, her biri sonrakine iz bırakan küçük kabullerin oluşturduğu bağımlı bir yol boyunca ilerler.
Arınma, insanın kendi başına sahip olduğu durağan temizlik değil, Allah'ın lütfuyla büyütüp geliştirdiği bir iyileşme sürecidir.
İzlenen küçük adımların, zamanla kişiyi kendi seçtiği yolun kıvrımlı bağına bağladığı düşünülebilir; ancak ip imgesi ayetin yüzeyinin zorunlu kıldığı bir anlam değildir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Moral deviation is spatially enacted as a traceable sequence and as distance maintained by a taut, crooked line.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Footprints, stepwise tracking, a long well-rope, and crooked tension separate the incremental mechanism of following from the deviant condition of the leader followed.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Stepwise Pursuit
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A walker places successive steps; another traces them one by one until the path produces a binding consequence.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:21 `لَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ ... وَمَن يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَاتِ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The warning describes a process with temporal granularity. Each small imitation supplies the location of the next; repeated following becomes continuity, and continuity leaves a liability behind it. The danger lies in the chain, not only its endpoint.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Long Tether of Rebellion
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A remote, rebellious agent pulls from a distance through a long, tightly twisted line whose crooked heading resists the intended course.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: remoteness and severance `quranic:root_000796:B001/m01`; long tightly twisted rope `quranic:root_000796:B002/m01`; crooked divergence and opposition `quranic:root_000796:B003/m01`; insolent rebel `quranic:root_000796:B004/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The satanic figure carries a mechanical image distinct from the follower's footsteps. Distance does not remove control: a long tether can transmit pull, and its crooked tension biases every subsequent step. The image materializes remote influence without collapsing it into compulsion.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali yalniz korkunun kalkmasi olarak degil, kalbin yatismasi, guven verme, guvenilirlik, emanet edilen sey, guvenli yer ve dayanilir nitelik alanlariyla birlikte verir. Bu nedenle dalin cercevesi, guvenlik ve guvenilirlik ekseninde hem yalın hem de yapimli ve baglamli kullanislari ayirt ederek korunabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal inanma ya da dua cevabi degil; korkudan emin olma, guven verme ve guvenilir sayilma alanidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalin guven ve korkusuzluk anlamlari ile belirli yapimli ya da soz obegi kullanislari birlikte vardir; tanim bunlari tek bir dar kaliba indirgemez.

concept_map.definition: Korkunun kalkmasiyla kalbin yatismasi, birine guven verilmesi veya bir kimsenin ya da seyin guvenilir kabul edilmesidir. Bu alan guvenli yer, emanet edilen sey, kendisine guvenilen kisi ve dayanilir binek gibi bagimli uygulamalari da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek korkuya karsi guven, ic yatiskinligi ve tehlikeden emin olma halidir.
Guven verme, birini kendi koruma ve teminat alani icine alma olarak kullanilir.
Guvenilirlik, ihanete karsi sadakat, emanet edilen sey ve kendisine guvenilen kisi anlamlarini dogurur.
Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.
Dayanikli ve aksamasindan korkulmayan deve kullanimi, guvenilirlik niteligini canli bir ornege uygular.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ortak olarak bu dali korkunun ziddi olan guven, kalbin yatismasi ve guven verme alaninda toplar. Ayni iddia guvenilir kisi, emanet, guvenli yer ve dayanilir binek gibi turemis ya da baglamli kullanislari da cekirdege baglar.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الأمن ضد الخوف، والأمان وإعطاء الأمنة، والأمانة ضد الخيانة وما اؤتمن عليه، والآمن والمأمن والاستئمان، والأمين والمأمون وما يوثق به، ومنه وثاقة الناقة الأمون.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس تصديق الإيمان من حيث هو تصديق، ولا صيغة آمين في الدعاء، ولا أمن المركبة من أم ومن في قوله أمن هو قانت.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الأمن ضد الخوف (ayn;sihah)؛ أصل الأمن طمأنينة النفس وزوال الخوف (mufradat)؛ الأمانة ضد الخيانة ومعناها سكون القلب (maqayis)؛ الأمان إعطاء الأمنة (maqayis;ayn)؛ أمن فلان يأمن أمنا وأمانا وأمنة فهو آمن (tahdhib)؛ استأمن إليه دخل في أمانه (sihah)؛ مأمنه منزله الذي فيه أمنه (mufradat)؛ الأمون الناقة الأمينة الوثيقة أو التي يؤمن فتورها وعثورها (ayn;sihah;mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali acikca tasdik, haber ya da vaadi dogru sayma ve bazi dini kullanislarda hakka boyun egme olarak verir. Provisional cerceve guvene dokunan yanini not eder, fakat dal kimligi korkusuzluk degil tasdik ve kabul iliskisidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal guvenlik hali degil; bir soz, haber, vaat veya hakikati dogru kabul etme alanidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Hem genel tasdik adlari hem de belirli soz obekleri ve dini kullanislar vardir; tanim bunlari yalin guven anlamina genisletmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir haber, vaat veya hakikati dogru sayip ona icten kabul ile yonelmektir. Dini kullanista bu kabul, kalp, dil ve davranisla baglanan bir boyun egme ya da seriate girme anlami kazanabilir.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek bir haberin, sozun veya hakikatin dogru sayilmasidir.
Hakka yonelik ic kabul, yalniz bilmekten ziyade boyun egme ve kabullenme bicimi alir.
Dini alanlarda bu kabul, bildirilen yola girme ve ona baglanma adi olarak kullanilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi veya onun bıraktığı belirtileri zaman içinde birbiri ardınca aramayı ve incelemeyi açıkça anlatır. Dalın aşamalı, araştırıcı ve iz odaklı çerçevesi bu kurucu özellikleri doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Sırf birinin arkasından yürümek ya da hızlıca yetişmek yeterli değildir; arama ve adım adım sürdürme gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel aşamalı arama biçimi ile özellikle iz ve belirtilerin tek tek incelendiği söz öbeği birbirine karıştırılmadan tanımlanır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi, bilgiyi ya da bırakılmış izleri arayarak zaman içinde parça parça ilerlemek; her yeni belirtiyi öncekinin ardından inceleyip araştırmayı sürdürmek.

facets.statement: Aranan şeyi zaman aralıkları içinde parça parça ve birbirini izleyen adımlarla araştırmak.
Bir kişi, olay veya bilginin bıraktığı iz ve belirtileri tek tek inceleyerek ilerlemek.
Bir kimsenin kusurlarını veya geride bıraktığı kayıt ve nesneleri ayrıntılı biçimde araştırmak.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak kanıt, arama eyleminin tek hamlede değil, zaman tanıyarak ve bir bulgudan ötekine geçerek yürütüldüğünü vurgular; izler, kusurlar ve kayıt parçaları bu yöntemin uygulama alanlarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin kendisini veya bıraktığı belirtileri zaman içinde tek tek arayıp inceleme sürecinin genel karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Aşamalı ilerlemeyi, aramayı ve birbirini izleyen belirtileri inceleme işlemini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Somut belirtiler, kayıtlar veya bir kişinin geride bıraktığı işaretler üzerinden ilerlenen araştırmalarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: İz dışındaki bir nesneyi genel olarak parça parça arama kapsamını daraltır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, eylem ve şeylerin araya boşluk girmeden birbirinin ardından gelmesini, anlatımın kesintisiz sürdürülmesini ve bir grubun ötekine ardışık biçimde eklenmesini anlatır. Dalın süreklilik ve ardışıklık çerçevesi bu ortak yapıyı doğru verir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Buradaki çekirdek kesintisiz ardışıklıktır; işin özenli yapılması veya bir hakkın istenmesi bu dala ait değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Ardışıklık bildiren biçimler ile iki eylemi aralıksız bağlayan söz öbeği ayrı yüzler olarak korunur; kapsam yalın köke genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Şeyleri, eylemleri veya anlatım bölümlerini araya kesinti koymadan birbirinin ardından getirmek ya da bunların bu biçimde peş peşe gerçekleşmesi.

facets.statement: Birden çok şeyin veya eylemin aralıksız biçimde birbirinin ardından gelmesi.
İki ibadet veya okuma eylemini araya boşluk koymadan peş peşe yapmak.
Bir anlatıyı bölmeden, bölümlerini birbirine bağlayarak sürdürmek.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar, ardışık öğeler arasında bekleme veya kopukluk bulunmamasını ortak özellik sayar; eylemleri peş peşe yapma, anlatıyı sürdürme ve grupları sırayla birbirine ekleme bu yapının görünümleridir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Şeylerin, eylemlerin veya anlatım parçalarının kesinti olmadan birbirini izlediği bütün çekirdek bağlamlarda kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir alacak, kan bedeli veya öç için istemde bulunmayı ve bunu yapan kişiyi destekler; ayrıca alacağın ödeme gücü olan başka bir kişiden alınmak üzere yönlendirilmesini anlatır. İlk olumsuz örnekte geçen yükümlülük ise komşu dalın sınırına aittir ve bu dalın çekirdeğine katılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: İstemde bulunan kişi ve alacağın başka ödeyene yöneltilmesi kapsamdadır; kişiye yüklenen olumsuz sonuç ayrı daldır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Hak isteyen kişi biçimi, belirli ödeme yönlendirmesi söz öbeği ve yerleşik biçimde hak istemeyi anlatan birim ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir alacak, kan bedeli, öç veya başka bir hak için karşı taraftan ödeme ya da karşılık istemek ve bu istemi yürüten kişi olmak. Belirli yapıda alacak, ödeme gücü olan başka bir kişiden alınmak üzere ona yöneltilir.

facets.statement: Bir hak, alacak, kan bedeli veya öç için karşı taraftan ödeme ya da karşılık istemek.
Bu istemi sürdüren hak veya alacak sahibini adlandırmak.
Belirli yapıda alacağı, ödeme gücü olan başka bir kişiden alınmak üzere o kişiye yöneltmek.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, hak veya alacak için istemde bulunma ile istem sahibini aynı alan içinde verir ve ödeme sorumluluğunun ödeme gücü bulunan başka bir kişiye yöneltildiği özel yapıyı da kaydeder. Yükümlülüğün kendisini anlatan olumsuz örnek, dal sınırını belirler.

facets.statement: İlk yaş yılı içindeki erkek sığır yavrusunu adlandırmak.
Aynı yaştaki dişi sığır yavrusunu ayrı bir biçimle adlandırmak.
Yavrusu arkasından gelen ineği belirli bir söz öbeğiyle nitelemek.
Otuz sığır üzerinden verilen yükümlülükte ilk yılındaki bir yavrunun alınması.
